lessons.title: Craters up close
lessons.brief: Big craters tell the Moon's story. Let's visit two of them.

facts.text: Copernicus is a crater about 96 km wide.

source.title: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Copernicus

facts.text: Shackleton crater is about 21 km wide. The south pole sits on its edge.

source.title: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Shackleton

steps.prompt: What made most of the round craters on the Moon?
steps.reveal: Space rocks. Each hit blasted out a round crater.
steps.hint: Think of things falling from space.

steps.prompt: Find Copernicus, a big sharp crater on the near side.
Which crater has the south pole on its edge?
steps.success: Correct. Shackleton, at the south pole.
steps.hint: It's the one at the very bottom.

steps.prompt: What do we call rock thrown out when a crater forms?
steps.success: Roger. Ejecta, the splash of rock.
steps.hint: It starts with e, like eject.
